cards.prose: The saying that had been handed down about killing stopped at the deed, and Moses had never stopped there. He had already put the commandment in the heart, in *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart*, so when Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of anger he is setting the sixth word back where it was given.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Moses forbids the hatred in the heart and the bearing of sin on a neighbour, which is where the sixth commandment was always rooted.

cards.prose: What was heard about adultery had been narrowed to the act. The tenth word of Moses names the wanting, so the look Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is the seventh commandment and the tenth kept side by side as they were given, with the heart as the place where both are broken first.
cards.member_phrase: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife
cards.member_sentence: The tenth commandment forbids coveting a neighbour's wife, so the Torah had already named the desire that comes before the act.

cards.prose: The writing of divorcement spoke of how a marriage is ended and never said what a marriage is. Here, at the very start, it is said: a man leaves his father and mother, cleaves to his wife, and the two are one flesh. That beginning is what Yahusha (Jesus) sets the question against.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The first marriage tells what a marriage is, one flesh from the beginning, and that is the measure for any talk of putting a wife away.

cards.prose: When the Pharisees pressed him, Yahusha (Jesus) told them what the writing of divorcement was. Moses suffered it because of hard hearts, and from the beginning it was not so. So he is not overturning Moses in the Sermon, he is pointing back past the allowance to the marriage as it began.
cards.member_phrase: Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) himself says Moses allowed the writing of divorcement because of hard hearts and that it was not so from the beginning.

cards.prose: What had been piled on the commandment about oaths shows plainly in the woes. A man who swore by the temple was said to owe nothing, while one who swore by its gold was bound. Yahusha (Jesus) is not striking down the oath Moses gave, he is clearing off the ladder of grades the scribes built on it.
cards.member_phrase: Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names the system of graded oaths the scribes taught, which is what the saying in the Sermon had grown into.

cards.prose: An eye for an eye was a measure for the judge, keeping payment to the size of the wrong, and Paul shows the ruler still holds that office, one who is *not a terror to good works* but to the evil. What Yahusha (Jesus) answers in the Sermon is the private man taking that measure into his own hand.
cards.member_phrase: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil
cards.member_sentence: Paul shows the ruler's office to punish evil still stands, so the Sermon speaks to the person wronged and not to the court.

cards.prose: The saying took the neighbour commandment and added *hate thine enemy* to it. Moses had written the opposite, setting the stranger who lives among them beside the native born and telling them to love him as themselves. Yahusha (Jesus) takes off what was added and gives back what Moses wrote.
cards.member_phrase: the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself
cards.member_sentence: Moses already extends the love command to the stranger dwelling with them, a part the added saying left out.

cards.prose: There is no word of Moses telling anyone to hate an enemy, and the law says the plain opposite in work: find his ox wandering and take it back to him. Whoever tacked *hate thine enemy* onto the neighbour commandment was laying something on top of it, and Yahusha (Jesus) lifts it off.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The Torah commands a hand of help toward an enemy's straying animal, and nowhere commands hatred of an enemy.

cards.prose: Solomon's proverb already put love for an enemy into bread and water, feeding the one who hungers and giving drink to the one who thirsts. Those who knew the Proverbs had not been taught to hate their enemies, and Yahusha (Jesus) speaks the same word they had open before them.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The Proverbs tell the reader to feed a hungry enemy and give him water, which is love for an enemy shown in deed.

cards.prose: Abram heard *walk before me, and be thou perfect* from Yahuah (the LORD) long before the Sermon, and the Father who is perfect is the measure in both places. So the perfection asked on the mountain is the whole, upright walk Elohim (God) asked of Abram, not some new height.
cards.member_phrase: I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) told Abram to walk before him and be perfect, the same standard the Sermon closes on.

cards.prose: The poor in spirit are the very people Yahuah (the LORD) says he dwells with, the One who inhabits eternity keeping company with the contrite and the humble. Since the kingdom is theirs, it is no surprise that the same verse promises to revive them.
cards.member_phrase: I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit
cards.member_sentence: The high and holy One says he dwells with the contrite and humble spirit and revives it.

cards.prose: The mourners here are not only sad. They are the men *that sigh and that cry for all the abominations*, and Yahuah (the LORD) marks them before the sword goes through the city. The comfort Yahusha (Jesus) promises belongs to that grief over what is done against Elohim (God).
cards.member_phrase: set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations
cards.member_sentence: Those who sigh and cry over the abominations in the city are the ones Yahuah (the LORD) sets his mark upon.

cards.prose: To hunger and thirst after righteousness is the longing of the hart at the water brooks, a soul crying for Elohim (God) himself. The promise that *they shall be filled* is the answer to that panting.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist's soul pants after Elohim (God) like a deer after water, the thirst the Beatitude pronounces blessed.

cards.prose: The righteousness the hungry are filled with comes from the righteous Branch raised to David, and Yahusha (Jesus) is that Branch speaking on the mountain. His name is *Yahuah Tsidkenu (THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS)* (Jeremiah 23:6), which tells what the hungry are filled with.
cards.member_phrase: I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper
cards.member_sentence: A righteous Branch is raised to David to reign and execute judgment and justice, the source of the righteousness the hungry are filled with.

cards.prose: The question of who shall stand in the holy place is answered right there: *He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart* (Psalm 24:4). Yahusha (Jesus) takes up that same answer, and the pure in heart who see Elohim (God) are the ones who stand in his place.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The question of who may ascend Yahuah's (the LORD's) hill and stand in his holy place is the one the pure in heart answer.

cards.prose: A pure heart is a heart where the law is written. Yahuah (the LORD) promises to put his law in the inward parts of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same law set inside, so those who are pure in heart see Elohim (God) because the commandment is in them where he put it.
cards.member_phrase: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to write his law in the hearts of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the source of a pure heart.

cards.prose: Who can be pure in heart? Here Yahuah (the LORD) promises to take away the stony heart and give a heart of flesh. The pure heart is something he gives to the scattered he gathers home, and the next words say what it is for: *cause you to walk in my statutes* (Ezekiel 36:27).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a heart of flesh, the gift from which the pure in heart come.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) said of his servant that *he will magnify the law, and make it honourable*, and that is the work Yahusha (Jesus) says he has come to do. To fulfil the law, as he means it, is to make it great and honourable, which is the opposite of destroying it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The servant of Yahuah (the LORD) is promised to magnify the law and make it honourable, which is what fulfilling it means.

cards.prose: Luke has the saying on the same ground. The one who says he did not come to destroy is the one who says the smallest stroke of the law will outlast the sky and the ground under it, so both gospels hand the law to the reader whole and standing.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Luke records the same saying, that the smallest stroke of the law fails more slowly than heaven and earth pass.

cards.prose: Matthew says the one who breaks the least commandment and teaches others to do so is called least, and James says the same from the other side: the law is one, and offending in a single point reaches the whole of it. Neither leaves a small commandment lying loose for a man to drop.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: James says whoever offends in one point of the law is guilty of all, so even the least commandment cannot be dropped.

cards.prose: Peter puts the last word of the Sermon in the same pattern the Torah uses, the one who called you being holy and you being holy as he is. Matthew says perfect as your Father is perfect, and in both places the measure is the Father himself and not a new rule.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Peter carries forward the same standard, that those called are to be holy as the one who called them is holy.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says through Malachi that he *hateth putting away*, and what he names is treachery against the wife of a man's covenant. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks the same way about the man who puts his wife away, so his word stands on this one and does not step off it.
cards.member_phrase: saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says he hates putting away and calls it treachery, the ground Yahusha's (Jesus's) word on divorce stands on.
